container_type: MP4 / ISO Base Media File Format (incl. MOV)

findings.description: 625 byte(s) follow the end of the last top-level box and are not part of any declared box.
findings.significance: Data appended after the final box is outside the ISO-BMFF structure. Small amounts can be benign padding, but appended data is a documented concealment technique and should be examined (e.g. hex-inspected) to determine its content.
findings.standard: ISO/IEC 14496-12 §4.2 (file is a sequence of boxes); Hall (2015), Analysis of MP4 Container File Format Forensics
findings.title: Data present after last top-level box

findings.description: The parser encountered a structure that deviates from ISO/IEC 14496-12.
findings.detail: offset=2192783: Box 'îþ|' declares size 346733863 extending to offset 348926646, beyond its container end 2193408. Treated as truncated.
findings.significance: A file that cannot be parsed strictly per the specification is itself a forensic finding; it may be truncated, malformed, or non-standard.
findings.title: Container parse deviation

findings.description: The container signature is most similar to the 'FFmpeg Re-encoded' profile. This is a similarity score against documented profiles, not a device identification.
findings.detail: similarity_score=4; compatible brands overlap ['isom']; video codec 'hvc1' matches; audio codec 'mp4a' matches  | notes: FFmpeg-encoded files are identifiable by Lavf/Lavc encoder strings in udta metadata and characteristic timescale values. Presence indicates post-processing (which many tools perform under the hood), not necessarily content manipulation.
findings.significance: The closest profile corresponds to re-encoding/editing software, which indicates the file passed through post-processing (not necessarily content manipulation).
findings.standard: Hall (2015), Analysis of MP4 Container File Format Forensics; device_db v1.1.1; sources: Hall 2015, FFmpeg documentation, published forensic literature on re-encoded media
findings.title: Closest device-class profile: FFmpeg Re-encoded

findings.description: One or more boxes carry zero creation/modification times (1904-01-01 epoch).
findings.significance: Zero timestamps mean the recording device did not set a clock. Documented but not an anomaly alone — common on dashcams and some action cameras.
findings.title: Zero (epoch) timestamps present

findings.description: Track 2 (soun) track(tkhd) duration differs from movie duration by more than tolerance.
findings.significance: Durations that do not reconcile across mvhd, tkhd and mdhd are documented in Hall (2015) as indicators of assembled or trimmed content. Small differences can be benign (edit lists, differing track lengths).
findings.standard: ISO/IEC 14496-12 §8.2.2, §8.3.2, §8.4.2; Hall (2015), Analysis of MP4 Container File Format Forensics
findings.title: Duration mismatch across boxes

findings.description: Track 2 (soun) media(mdhd) duration differs from movie duration by more than tolerance.
findings.significance: Durations that do not reconcile across mvhd, tkhd and mdhd are documented in Hall (2015) as indicators of assembled or trimmed content. Small differences can be benign (edit lists, differing track lengths).
findings.standard: ISO/IEC 14496-12 §8.2.2, §8.3.2, §8.4.2; Hall (2015), Analysis of MP4 Container File Format Forensics
findings.title: Duration mismatch across boxes

findings.description: Track 1 (vide) uses a 64-bit co64 offset table although the file is under 4 GB.
findings.significance: Direct camera recordings under 4 GB normally use 32-bit stco. co64 here may indicate a writer/muxer that defaults to 64-bit offsets.
findings.standard: ISO/IEC 14496-12 §8.7.5; Hall (2015), Analysis of MP4 Container File Format Forensics
findings.title: 64-bit offset table (co64) in a sub-4GB file

findings.description: Track 2 (soun) uses a 64-bit co64 offset table although the file is under 4 GB.
findings.significance: Direct camera recordings under 4 GB normally use 32-bit stco. co64 here may indicate a writer/muxer that defaults to 64-bit offsets.
findings.standard: ISO/IEC 14496-12 §8.7.5; Hall (2015), Analysis of MP4 Container File Format Forensics
findings.title: 64-bit offset table (co64) in a sub-4GB file
